candidates.source_name: 1 Enoch (Ethiopian tradition) / Epistle of Enoch (1 Enoch 91-108)
candidates.draft_body:
1 Enoch (Ethiopian tradition) Epistle of Enoch (1 Enoch 91-108) (c. 100 BC)

'I have sworn unto you, ye sinners, as a mountain has not become a slave, and a hill does not become the handmaid of a woman, even so sin has not been sent upon the earth, but man of himself has created it' — the human authorship of sin. Tewahedo theodicy preserves this verse as the FOUNDATIONAL anti-Manichaean text: evil is not co-eternal substance, not divinely sent, not natural — humans authored it. Cited in Tewahedo anti-Manichaean polemic against the Zandic dualism that periodically appeared in Ethiopian church history.

Verify the summary still reflects the source's argument before promoting; substitute a verbatim quote from the NPNF / Charles dump where available, and where applicable cross-check the Andəmta homiletic tradition for resonance.

candidates.source_name: 1 Enoch (Ethiopian tradition) / Epistle of Enoch (1 Enoch 91-108)
candidates.draft_body:
1 Enoch (Ethiopian tradition) Epistle of Enoch (1 Enoch 91-108) (c. 100 BC)

'And now know ye that from the angels He will inquire as to your deeds in heaven, from the sun and from the moon and from the stars in reference to your sins because upon the earth ye execute judgement on the righteous. And He will summon to testify against you every cloud and mist and dew and rain' — the entire cosmos as witness against sinners. Tewahedo cosmic-conscience theology preserves this image: every element of creation is morally aware and records human deeds — parallel to Hab 2:11 ('the stone shall cry out of the wall').

'I have sworn unto you, ye sinners, as a mountain has not become a slave, and a hill does not become the handmaid of a woman, even so sin has not been sent upon the earth, but man of himself has created it' — the human authorship of sin. Tewahedo theodicy preserves this verse as the FOUNDATIONAL anti-Manichaean text: evil is not co-eternal substance, not divinely sent, not natural — humans authored it. Cited in Tewahedo anti-Manichaean polemic against the Zandic dualism that periodically appeared in Ethiopian church history.

1 Enoch (Ethiopian tradition) Epistle of Enoch (1 Enoch 91-108) (c. 100 BC)

'And now know ye that from the angels He will inquire as to your deeds in heaven, from the sun and from the moon and from the stars in reference to your sins because upon the earth ye execute judgement on the righteous. And He will summon to testify against you every cloud and mist and dew and rain' — the entire cosmos as witness against sinners. Tewahedo cosmic-conscience theology preserves this image: every element of creation is morally aware and records human deeds — parallel to Hab 2:11 ('the stone shall cry out of the wall').
